answer: Trust propagates through an attestation graph by bounded random walks, so voting weight reflects reachable, independently supported paths rather than raw identities. If a sybil cluster has only a sparse external cut, its low conductance limits probability flow into it; with normalized edge weights and bounded walk length, its aggregate influence is bounded by cut capacity and ingress from honest nodes. Willow, signal, and jetty can denote boundary attestations, not extra votes.
